## 4 Editing

### 4.1 The declarations — the ops of `setMassing` and `setComposition`

Item 101's rule is kept: no thirteenth tool. The building tool T9 `shape` (L3) gains parameters, each an existing
event or one of the two event kinds `setMassing` and `setComposition` that §7.1 declares (item 351); this section
declares their ops. A new building is still T6 `place` / `build`, whose S11 run is the massing.

```ts
type MassingOp =
  | { op: 'family'; family: MassingFamilyId }                                                   // re-lay the building as another family: V02 §3.9 W1–W9 with that family, the current wings the seeds; draws on siteplan.mutate (V02 §3.12)
  | { op: 'addRange'; from: PointsForm /* two points: the range's centre line (item 101 (i)) */; widthCm?: Cm; floors?: number; role?: 'range' | 'cross' | 'service' }
  | { op: 'reshapeRange'; wing: number /* key */; ends?: [PointCm, PointCm]; widthCm?: Cm }    // the centre-line and width handles
  | { op: 'addTower'; from: PointsForm /* one point: the centre */; radiusCm?: Cm; shape?: 'round' | 'square' | 'octagon'; turret?: boolean; floors?: number }
  | { op: 'moveTower'; wing: number; at: PointCm; radiusCm?: Cm; shape?: 'round' | 'square' | 'octagon' }   // shape: the ring re-made at the same centre and radius
  | { op: 'addBlock'; wing: number /* the host range */; at: PointCm /* on its ridge */; lengthCm?: Cm; depthCm?: Cm }
  | { op: 'backRange'; on: boolean; lengthCm?: Cm; widthCm?: Cm; side?: 'left' | 'right' }
  | { op: 'removeWing'; wing: number }
  | TiersOp;                                                                                     // V02 §4.6
type CompositionOp =
  | { op: 'dormers'; wing: number; eave: 0 | 1; count: number; widthCm?: Cm; kind?: DormerKind }
  | { op: 'porch'; kind: PorchKind | 'none'; widthCm?: Cm; depthCm?: Cm; entrance?: number /* an Entrance ordinal: set → the secondary porch at that side, rear or yard entrance (a hood or none) */ }
  | { op: 'room'; role: 'hall' | 'gatehall' | 'chapel'; on: boolean; fromCm?: Cm; toCm?: Cm /* the extent along its host's ridge, from the host's ridge start */ };   // V02 §3.8's rooms: on or off, and their extent
```

Storeys and roofs of one wing are the base's `setAttr` on `wings/<key>/heights/floors` and `wings/<key>/roof` (`kind`,
`pitch`, `high`), addressed by key (§7.1; item 351). A lock on `wings/<key>` (an attribute-level lock, §7.2) holds that
wing against every mutation, re-derivation and edit of another wing. Re-rolls are the base's `regenerate` with `rung:
'wings'` or `'rooms'`; the massing's re-roll is New random on the building's plot. **Draws** (J-V2.18; V02 §3.12): the
geometric ops draw nothing — a default an op leaves out is the row's deterministic central value (the midpoint of a range
cell, the heaviest weight of a weighted one); the `family` op draws on `siteplan.mutate`, a pure function of its key, so a
replay is exact either way.

**No refusal but a lock or a dossier fact** (item 101 R2; J-V2.79; J-VI.4). Every infeasible op of this section and of
V02 §4.6 is **bent** to the nearest lawful one and named in one line with its closest alternatives, under an id of
V02 §1b's bend row (`bend.<…>` below); V09 §4.9 words each id and V10's clerk says it (X21, X22). A bend draws nothing
(V02 §3.12), is one undoable event, and replays from a skeleton file to the same bend. An op on a locked wing, or one that
would move a locked wing, is refused with the lock named; with a dossier fact (item 20) these are the only refusals.

### 4.2 What each `setMassing` does — dry run, commit, locality, undo

1. **The new wing set, as values.** `family`: V02 §3.9's steps, recorded as `MutationStep`s in `EditBase.mutations`; a
   `family` op into or out of `stepped` also writes the use's stepped specialisation in the same undo group (V02 §4.6 (1)).
   `addRange`: the points form's two points (snapped; the authoring boundary's resampling and snap, §7.1) are the centre
   line; width as given or the row's middle width; an end within `w` of another range's long side ends on that side (a
   butt joint, the new range abutting); an end within `w/2` of another range's free end, turned by more than 2°,
   mitres with it; role `range` unless given; floors as given or the `main` wing's; roof by the role's default kind.
   `reshapeRange`: the ends and width move; every range abutting it is re-trimmed to its new side; a block on it is
   re-split (V02 §3.5 M7). `addTower`: the one point is the centre; radius and shape as given or the row's middle; floors
   one above the tallest wing it meets. `moveTower`: the same tests at the new centre; a new `shape` re-makes the ring at
   the same centre and radius (the room and stair of a stored plan re-cut by the plan rung). `addBlock`: V02 §3.5 M7 on
   the host at the given point. `backRange`: V02 §3.5 M9 on or off with the given sizes and side. `removeWing`: the wing
   leaves (its key is never re-used); a removed block's host pieces re-join into one wing that keeps the lowest of their
   keys; **removing the `main` wing passes the role to the longest remaining range** (ties by key). The bends of this step:
   * `removeWing` of the building's last wing → T6's `remove` of the building, one undoable event (`bend.building.remove`:
     "Removed the building with its last wing");
   * `reshapeRange` on a row quad — whose party walls are the plot's (J-V2.13) — for its ends' moves along the frontage →
     the plot edit that moves that party-wall line: the plot's `moveVertex` on the line's frontage vertex, the neighbour's
     quad re-clipped by S11, both in one event (`bend.row.plotLine`; a lock on the neighbour's quad or plot is refused
     with the lock named, R2's second class); for its width (the quad's depth into the plot) the op re-cuts the quad's
     rear chain at the new depth inside the plot and the back region, the quad then an edited, pinned wing;
   * `removeWing` on a row quad that is not the building's last wing removes it — a gap in the row, the neighbours'
     party-wall ends reclassed as gables by the roofscape (V02 §5.2 step 1), the remaining wing taking `main`;
   * a `family` op whose family is unreachable or infeasible on the building → the reachable, feasible family nearest
     it — the fewest growth-lattice steps, ties by the target row's weight — naming the least plot the asked family needs
     and offering `join` (`bend.family.nearest`).

   Every writer re-sorts the wings into the canonical order (V02 §2.1) and rewrites `MassingRef.segments` before the dry
   run's checks.
2. **The dry run** (on the overlay, §7.1): the region the edit may use is the plot less the footprints of the plot's
   other buildings, each buffered by `attractCm` (§3.2) — so a hand may build to the plot line, never over a neighbour, a
   passage's other side or a way. The checks are V02 §3.5 M13's (tiling apart from towers, containment in that region, the
   ring rules, `minEdge`) and M8 (ii)–(v) for any tower; M10's budget is not applied to a hand edit (the capacity follows
   the shell). A failing op is bent to the nearest lawful one: a range crossing the region's boundary, or an op reaching
   beyond the plot, is clipped to it, the line offering `join` with the neighbour (T9's `join`, §7.1) as the way to more
   land (`bend.wing.clip`); a tower that would stand through a wing moves outward along the line from the wing's nearest
   boundary point by the least distance that passes (iii) (`bend.tower.move`); a range overlapping another is trimmed to a
   butt joint (`bend.wing.trim`); a wing below 4 m² or with a side below `minEdge` is grown about its centre line to the
   least lawful size — its width first to 2 m, then its length until 4 m² — inside the region (`bend.wing.grow`). **The
   dry run also lists**, from V03's `plan` query, every stored-plan room, edited opening and furnished room the op would
   orphan (V03 §3.11, V03 §4.3), each with §7.3's orphan actions — the `tiers` op's dry run among them.
3. **The commit** runs S11's operator on the plot with the building's new wings as fixed (the path `moveFootprint`
   already takes, §2.6 rule 5): the footprint face re-inserted with the plot's other buildings fixed, `deriveBase`, the
   entrance set re-derived (an edited entrance kept, §7.2; the massing's entrance hint re-read), the basement re-derived
   unless edited — **keeping the crypt** of an `always` class with no condition, and a `basement`-class church's while its
   class stays in the church family, the cathedral's by the no-refusal ladder and its wet-ground lift (V02 §3.14.5) — the
   yard partition re-fitted (a new hole typed `court`, item 303), the capacity function re-read and any excess re-homed by
   §4.7's overflow pass, the first carry; for a stored composition, its re-match by key (V02 §3.9 W8); a **stored plan is
   re-cut inside the event** by V03 §3.11 around its edited parts. An unstored `wings` rung is marked stale.
4. **Locality (§7.3 item 1).** The effective scope is the plot (its faces and buildings), the passage a wing spans
   (the base's rule) and the buildings receiving re-homed households; T-V2-19 checks that nothing else changes.
5. **Undo** keeps the former wings, `Building.massing`, `nextWingKey`, the stored composition and everything S11's
   re-fit changed (§7.4's S11 rows); undo restores them exactly, a re-homed household's former building included.

### 4.3 What each `setComposition` does

The first `setComposition` on a building **stores its composition** — the current derived composition, with the op
applied — as `Building.composition` (§2.6's rule for the first composition or plan edit), its record `edited`.

* `dormers`: the count is clamped to the eave's bays (`facadeBays`, V02 §3.7) and named when clamped
  (`bend.dormers.count`); the row is marked `edited` (a fixed input to the plan rung's dormers, V03).
* `porch`: a kind whose space fails (V02 §3.7) is bent to the nearest feasible kind; with `entrance` the op sets or
  removes the secondary porch there, a hood — any other kind there is bent to a hood (`bend.porch.kind` for both).
* `room`: turns the hall, the gate hall or the chapel on or off and sets its extent along its host's ridge, bent to the
  nearest lawful extent by V02 §3.13 (3)'s rule (`bend.room.extent`); the room is marked `edited` (a fixed ring for the
  plan rung) and kept through a re-derivation of the `rooms` rung while its host keeps its key; a stored plan is re-cut
  inside the event by V03 §3.11, the dry run listing what the op would orphan as V02 §4.2 step 2 does. Turning a room on
  where no host admits it bends: a gate hall without a `gate` range becomes a **gate passage** through the wing carrying
  the main entrance — from eave side to eave side at the entrance's offset, the row's central `gateHallM` wide, its two
  ends arches to the street and to the yard behind (`bend.room.passage`); a hall or chapel goes to the `main` wing, else
  the largest storeyed wing (a chapel at its east end by V02 §3.8's rule); on a building whose wings are all solid, the op
  first turns the tiers above tier 0 storeyed (the `tiers` op's `solid: 'lower'`, V02 §4.6) and then places the room in
  the lowest of them (`bend.room.host` for both, each step named).

The effective scope is the building. Undo restores the former composition, or removes the stored one when this event
stored it (J-P48 (5)); the rooms and plan points the stored composition holds are carried by `carryWings` (§2.6); its
composed wings and towers follow their base wings by key (V02 §2.2).

### 4.4 Lifecycle, orphans and the control

**Lifecycle.** The two kinds' row is §7.4's `setMassing / setComposition` row (item 351); the `tiers` op and every bend of
this section fall under it unchanged. What this volume adds to the row: an edited dormer row is also a fixed input to the
plan rung (V03); a secondary porch migrates by its entrance ordinal.

**Orphans (§7.3's orphan table; J-P48).** An edited dormer row whose eave changed length by more than ± 10 % (V02 §3.9 W8),
an edited room whose host key left, and a secondary porch whose entrance left are listed in §7.3's orphan table with two
actions: **re-attach** (a dormer row to the same eave of the same key, its count clamped to the new bays; a room to its
role's lawful host by V02 §3.8, its extent clamped; a porch to the nearest side, rear or yard entrance) and **discard**
(the derived value returns). Nothing orphaned is dropped silently.

**The control.** `fantasyShapes` is §7.8's stage-3 model control (item 402; documentation anchor V02 §3.3), in the
advanced panel. The `FM` building look (V02 §3.10.8) is a style choice for V09's style panel (X10); it changes no model
byte.

### 4.5 The canvas, the clerk and the skeleton file

* **Canvas handles** — V09 draws them (V09 §3.5; T-V9-42); this is their contract: at the building band, each range shows
  its two centre-line end handles and one width handle (drag → `reshapeRange`), each tower its centre and radius handles
  (→ `moveTower`) and a shape chip (→ `moveTower { shape }`), each wing a storey stepper and a roof-kind chip
  (→ `setAttr`), each eave a dormer stepper (→ `setComposition dormers`), the main entrance a porch chip and every side,
  rear or yard entrance a hood toggle (→ `setComposition porch`), and — at the building band with the plan shown — the
  hall, gate hall and chapel an on/off chip and two extent handles along their host's ridge (→ `setComposition room`); a
  **family strip** shows the feasible families of the building's row, each as a ghost made by a dry run of `setMassing
  family`, one tap committing it. Every drag previews its dry run live inside the plot (§14's interaction contract) and
  commits one event on release.
* **The clerk** (V10) calls the same operations through the tool API (§11.2): "make the manor an H" is
  `setMassing { family: 'H' }`; "a round tower on the north-east corner" is `addTower` with that corner's point;
  "two dormers on the street side" is `setComposition dormers` on the `main` wing's street eave. It reads a building's
  massing (family, wings with roles, storeys, roof kinds, towers) and composition (dormer rows, porch, rooms) through the
  reader, under §9.2's knowledge rules — the mass of every building is public (J-A30.83), and nothing in this volume is
  concealed (a front's concealed rooms are the plan's, V03).
* **"Why is it this shape?" — the `WhyProvider`** (J-V2.51; the why query is V10 §3.9's). `@plat/buildings` registers a
  provider for the kind `building` at the paths `massing`, `wings/<key>` and `composition`. It fills V10's `WhyAnswer`
  without a new field: **`facts`** — `massing/family`, `massing/row` (the key the chain reached), the manifested band and
  value, the drift bounds, `fantasyShapes`, `massing/segments`, `massing/axis` with `MassingRef.low`, each wing's role,
  floors and roof, and the **alternatives** as fact rows — `massing/alternatives/<family>` = its renormalised weight among
  M3's feasible families (or `infeasible: <the failed test>`), `wings/<key>/rejected/<i>` = the M8 test (i)–(v) a
  rejected tower candidate failed, `composition/porch/d` and `composition/porch/feasible`,
  `composition/dormers/<key>/<eave>/dropped` = the obstacle of a dropped dormer — each with `tier: 'derived'` and `row`
  the `composition.json` slice; **`cause`** — S11's massing (`step: 'S11'`, `rule: 'V02 §3.5'`, `chance: 'massing'` with
  its creation index), the `setMassing` event (`seq`), or the mutation's W1 draw or kept seeds (W2; `chance:
  'siteplan.mutate'`); the sunlit choice names `sunBias` and the options' factors; each bend taken is the fact
  `massing/bend/<id>`. The alternatives are **recomputed** by re-running M3 and the M5/M8 tests on the committed state
  without advancing any stream (a pure function), so the answer on an untouched building equals the massing's recorded
  draws (T-V2-43). "Why no crypt / why this crypt" is V03's and V04's provider (item 238's `Basement.crypt`).
* **A skeleton file** carries these events as ordered declarations like any other (§11.1): a building declared with
  `build` then shaped by `setMassing` lines is re-created exactly by the creation prefix's fold (§4.1's read-ahead reads
  no stage-3 declaration ahead; the massing runs when its plot's S11 runs, and the declared ops apply at their log
  positions).

### 4.6 Editing stacks and deck buildings

```ts
type TiersOp = { op: 'tiers'; count?: number; insetCm?: Cm; top?: 'flat' | 'shrine' | 'roofed'; stairs?: 'axial' | 'flights' | 'internal' | 'none';
    stairWidthCm?: Cm; shape?: 'rect' | 'round' | 'octagon'; lowerRoof?: 'flat' | 'pent'; solid?: 'all' | 'lower' | 'none';
    shrineInsetShare?: number; centre?: PointCm; radiusCm?: Cm };
    // re-lay a stepped building's stack on its tier 0 (layTiers' anchored mode); on any other building it first bends to family 'stepped'
```

Every limit of a stack, a deck or a row below is a bend under V02 §4.1's rule; undo restores the building's leaf digest
exactly.

1. **The `tiers` op.** On a building that is **not stepped** it bends to `setMassing { op: 'family', family: 'stepped' }`
   followed in the same event by the op's values (`bend.tiers.stepped`: "Made it a stepped building first") — V02 §3.15.5's
   anchored `single → stepped` on the building's `main` range, through `single` by the growth rows, drawing on
   `siteplan.mutate` as a `family` op does; where W1's anchored test fails, `bend.family.nearest` (V02 §4.2) applies.
   **The stepped specialisation (J-V2.94).** This bend, and a `setMassing { family: 'stepped' }` op, write in the same undo
   group (§7.1's `EditBase.group`) an `editTable` row op on the use's `siting.declared` `use:` row (V11 §4.2), setting its
   cell `specialisation` to the id of V11 §3.24.3's row for the use's culture and class where one exists, else
   `stepped_temple` for a class of the worship family, `terraced_palace` for `palace`, `tiered_tower` for `tower_house`,
   `mage_tower` or `watchtower`, and no cell for any other class (its own plan rows stay) — so `Use.specialisation`, the
   heights row where the specialisation names one (`stepped-shrine`) and V03's plan rows follow the hand-made stack, held
   and exempt from the chance and the cap (V11 §3.24.3). A `family` op from `stepped` to another family on a use holding a
   stepped specialisation writes `specialisation: 'none'` the same way. Undo removes the row op with the event; a skeleton
   file replays both lines.
   **On a stepped building** the `tiers` op re-runs `layTiers` in anchored mode on tier 0 with `MassingRef.stack` and the
   op's values, with no draw: a value the op leaves out keeps the stored one (the count: the tiers now standing; the step
   `stack.insetCm`; the grade `stack.grade`; the top; the stair form; the stair width: the current stairs'; the shape, the
   skirt, the solid mode and the shrine's inset as laid). **A new tier** takes the row's central values:
   `floors = max(1, round-half-up(central(tierFloors) × taper^k))`, or height `central(solidHeightM) × taper^k` to the
   centimetre. **Keys:** a kept tier keeps its key, and its ring and heights exactly where the step, the shape and the
   stair form are unchanged (else its ring is re-inset, its key and heights kept); a stair keeps its key across a change of
   stair form while its tier stands (its ring re-laid), and is removed with its tier or under `internal` or `none`; tiers
   above the new count are removed with their stairs and every wing standing on them (keys retired); new tiers and stairs
   take keys from `nextWingKey`; the shrine comes and goes with `top`.
   **The fields and their bends:**
   * `count` above what fits → the most that fits (`bend.tiers.count`); `insetCm` that leaves no second tier → the
     largest lawful step (`bend.tiers.step`).
   * `stairs`: `flights` on a round or octagonal stack → `axial` (`bend.tiers.axial`); **`internal` over a solid tier
     0** → `none` where every tier is solid, else `axial` (the first form of J-V2.74's order; `bend.tiers.none`,
     `bend.tiers.axial`); `none` over a storeyed tier 0 → `internal` (`bend.tiers.internal`); where the reserve of the
     asked form does not fit in front of tier 0 inside the plot, the forms are tried in J-V2.74's order, and where none
     fits the current form is kept, named with the depth the asked form needs (`bend.tiers.form`).
   * **`none` — the sealed stack:** lawful wherever tier 0 is solid; ST3 uses `d` on every side, ST5 lays no stair, ST6
     skips the chain check, `stairChain` is empty and `landingSide` null; a storeyed tier or shrine on it is reached by
     nothing (V03's `W_TIER_UNREACHED`), which the line names.
   * `shape` re-lays tier 0 as the named shape inscribed in its current ring's bounding rectangle in the building's frame
     (a round or octagonal ring at that rectangle's inradius, a rect at the rectangle itself), the stack re-inset.
   * `centre` and `radiusCm` (a round or octagonal tier 0): tier 0 re-laid as the regular ring of that centre and
     circumradius, clipped by the least move to the plot region (V02 §4.2 step 2), the stack re-inset.
   * `lowerRoof: 'pent'` → `flat` where the stair form is not `internal` or `none` (equal insets; `bend.stack.roof`); a
     stair form turned `axial` or `flights` on a pent stack turns its lower roofs `flat` in the same event, named
     (`bend.stack.roof`).
   * `solid`: `'all'`, `'lower'` or `'none'`; a tier turning storeyed takes the row's central floors (round-half-up), one
     turning solid keeps its `eaveCm` (less any parapet) as its height; a stair form made unlawful by it bends by the rules
     above (`internal` over a solid tier 0; `none` over a storeyed one).
   * `shrineInsetShare` re-lays the shrine (ST4's tests); a shrine that no longer fits drops the top to `flat`
     (`bend.tiers.top`).
2. **A tier's height.** `setAttr(wings/<key>/heights/floors)` on a storeyed tier or the shrine,
   `setAttr(wings/<key>/heights/eaveCm)` on a solid tier (item 351's paths). Inside the same event `rebaseStack` re-bases
   every wing standing on it, directly or through the chain, and each stair whose rise changed is re-laid (ST5, its width
   kept): where the terrace no longer holds the run at the stack's grade, the grade steepens up to `stairGradeMax`; beyond
   that the height is bent to the most the terrace allows (`bend.tier.height`: "the stair up this tier needs room on the
   terrace below"). **`setAttr(wings/<key>/heights/baseCm)` on a wing with `on`** bends to the same change in the height
   of the wing it stands on — a solid support's `eaveCm` by the difference, a storeyed support's floors by
   `round-half-up(difference ÷ storeyCm.upper)` (a zero result a no-op, named) — then the rules above (`bend.stack.base`);
   a user's `baseCm` on a ground wing is kept (J-DET-24) and carries the stack through `rebaseStack`. From M3a to M6c the
   base's `setAttr` of a wing's heights (the wing's index, which equals its key) does the same through the base outline
   builder (item 229).
3. **Roofs on a stack.** `setAttr(wings/<key>/roof)` bends (`bend.stack.roof`): on a lower tier to `flat` or to its
   shape's pent kind (`hip` rect, `pyramid` octagon, `cone` round), the pent kind only under `internal` or `none` (else
   `flat`); on the top tier among `flat`, `hip` (rect), `pyramid` (octagon) and `cone` (round) — another kind bends to its
   shape's kind; on a stair to `shed`; on the shrine among the kinds of `TierCells.shrine.roofs`, else the first.
   `MassingRef.stack.lowerRoof` stays the laid default that a later `tiers` re-lay applies.
4. **The other `setMassing` ops on a stepped building.**
   * `reshapeRange` on tier 0 re-insets the whole stack from its new ring (keys kept; a tier that no longer fits removed
     with its stair and everything on it, named).
   * `removeWing` on **tier k ≥ 1** removes it, its stair (the stair whose `to` is tier k), every wing standing on it and
     every higher tier with its stair (named). `removeWing` on **tier 0** removes the stack — tier 0, every stair and
     every wing standing on it; any ground wings added beside it stay (the longest takes `main`, the family becomes
     `single`, `stack` is cleared), and with none left it bends to T6's `remove` of the building
     (`bend.building.remove`).
   * `removeWing` on **a stair** bends to `tiers { stairs: 'internal' }` where tier 0 is storeyed ("Removed the stairs; the
     tiers are now reached from inside"), else to `tiers { stairs: 'none' }` ("… the pyramid is sealed") —
     `bend.tiers.internal`, `bend.tiers.none`.
   * `addRange`, `addTower` and `backRange` are admitted as **ground wings** (no `on`; `bend.stack.groundWing` names the
     placement): each is laid by V02 §4.2's rules outside tier 0's ring, every stair's ring and stair 0's **approach
     strip** — the reserve's width, `landingM` deep in front of stair 0's foot (under `internal`, `landingM` in front of the
     main entrance; under `none`, no strip) — moved away from them by the least distance; a range ending within `w` of
     tier 0's side abuts it (a butt joint, rule 1's shared vertices), a back range takes tier 0 as its host (M9's rear
     side), and a tower passes M8's tests (ii)–(v) with tier 0 as its host wing and its ring clear of every wing standing
     on tier 0, every stair and the strip, its eave raised above tier 0's roof in its ring (M11). **`addBlock`** (a block
     splits a range, and a tier is not a range) bends to `addRange` of the block's size at the given point on the ground
     beside tier 0 (`bend.stack.groundWing`). M13's pairing then covers tier 0, stair 0 and the added wings; ST6's nesting
     is unchanged.
   * `family` runs V02 §3.15.5's rows.
5. **Deck buildings.** Every op works as on any building, inside the deck plot (V02 §4.2 step 2's region, which lies
   inside the deck's width); **a floors value above the deck's `maxFloors` is bent to it** ("a deck carries at most n
   storeys"; `bend.deck.floors`) — for `setAttr` of floors and `addRange`'s `floors` alike (J-V2.70); M10's budget is not
   applied to a hand edit (V02 §4.2), so the plot alone bounds the footprint; **a `family: 'stepped'` op on a deck building
   bends to `single`**, the deck's lawful family nearest a stepped mass (`bend.deck.single`: "A bridge carries small, light
   buildings" — the deck's kind named). A hand placement of a crypt-bound use on a deck plot bends to the landward land
   plot (V02 §3.16 (6); T6's landward bend, V09's `bend.deck.class`).
6. **Locality, undo, lifecycle.** As V02 §4.2 (4)–(5): the effective scope is the plot (a `bend.row.plotLine` adds the
   neighbour's plot, both in one event); a stack's re-base and re-lay stay inside the building. The undo record keeps the
   former wings, `nextWingKey` and `MassingRef.stack`. §7.4's row (V02 §4.4) covers the `tiers` op and its bends, and a
   skeleton file carries `tiers` lines like any other `setMassing` line (a bent line replays to the same bend).
7. **The clerk, the canvas, the registry and "why".** "Give the temple five tiers" is `tiers { count: 5 }`; "a shrine on
   top" `tiers { top: 'shrine' }`; "stairs along the faces" `tiers { stairs: 'flights' }`; "seal it" `tiers { stairs:
   'none' }`; "make it round" `tiers { shape: 'round' }`; "skirt roofs on every tier" `tiers { lowerRoof: 'pent' }`; "one
   more storey on the second terrace" `setAttr(wings/<key>/heights/floors)` (V10; X22). V09 draws, at the building band, a
   tier stepper, a step handle on tier 1's front face, stair-form, top-form, shape, skirt and solid chips, a shrine-inset
   handle, the centre and radius handles on a round or octagonal tier 0, and a storey or height stepper per tier (X21;
   V09 §4.20.5). The entity registry carries, as read-only paths for V10's providers and V09's panels, `massing/stack` —
   each tier's wing key in tier order — and, on a deck's host (a mole, pier, quay platform or bridge),
   `deck/landmarks/<head|mid>` naming its landmark plots (`DeckContext.landmark`; CVR-V10-8). The `WhyProvider`
   (V02 §4.5) adds the facts `massing/stack/*` (shape, the row's stair form and the one laid, lowerRoof, top, insetCm,
   grade, truncated, the drawn count, the derived aspect), `wings/<key>/on`, `wings/<key>/solid`, `massing/stairSteep` and
   each bend taken (`massing/bend/<id>`), and for a deck building `massing/deck` (the deck kind, its host, the budget band
   and `maxFloors`, and whether the fallback constants were read), each with its `composition.json` or V11 slice — no new
   `WhyAnswer` field.

## 5 Rendering, labels, exports

### 5.1 What each band draws (§8.5's bands, with stage 3)

| band | stage 3 draws | from |
|---|---|---|
| **city** | the massing as masses — the base's closing per block (§8.5 (2)): a courtyard building's court stays open when it is wider than the closing's 1.5 px (a court is a yard part, `ground` at this band); towers and cross-wings show in the mass's silhouette; no roof lines | model (eager) |
| **district** | footprints with outlines and entrance ticks (the base's), and the **roofscape of the massing** (V02 §5.2): ridges, hips, valleys, walls, tower roofs and spires, the cupola — drawn by the style's construction; an `arcade` wing's ground-storey outline dashed; no dormers or porches | model, drawn lazily per tile |
| **neighbourhood** | the district band's, plus — where the building's `wings` rung is current or stored — dormers, the entrance gable, the porch, and §8.10's decorative chimneys at the façade-bay lines (`hearths` of them; none once the plan rung exists, J-A28.85); the change marker on a stale building (§8.5) | model + the elaboration cache |
| **building** | the neighbourhood band's at full detail, and the plan storey by storey (V03); the other storeys' wing outlines faded beneath (the base's) | model + cache |

Under a Works (item 67) a building draws its wings at their stage heights and §8.2's `states` rows: `wallsRising` draws no
roofscape facet, `roofFramed` draws the roofscape's lines through §8.2's `frame` program without fill, a `decayed` or
`ruined` building (roof kind `none`) draws no facet — its walls by the `states` rows (a ruined landmark, V02 §3.14.2,
included). **A stack under Works** takes its stage heights from item 318's `heightsAt` — the stack rising in stack order,
a solid wing by courses of `storeyCm.upper`, no wing drawn or cast before its support reaches its eave, each stair rising
with the tier whose top it reaches, a demolition lowering in reverse (V02 §5.6); V06's Works read the same order (X23). A
building whose roof kind is `none` takes no dormer, porch or cupola drawing. Condition (`worn`, `neglected`) and material
stay texture and colour on the same facets (item 19).

### 5.2 The roofscape — one roof plan per building (item 406)

`roofscape(building, composition?)` returns planar, pairwise non-overlapping facets that together cover the footprint
(and a porch outside it). It is derived at read in the tile worker (drawing, float64, the renderer's CPU reference) and
in the generation worker (exports); it stores nothing and draws nothing from any stream.

1. **Ends (`resolveEnds`).** Each wing with a ridge has two **ends** — the ring sides its ridge meets (sides 1 and 3 for
   `ridgeAxis 0`, 2 and 4 for 1). Each end is classed, in this order: `open` if a tower ring covers it; `party` if it lies
   on a party-wall edge of the plot (a row quad's side); `mitre` if it is shared vertex for vertex with another wing's
   end; if it lies along another wing `Y`'s side (a butt joint): `wall` when `Y.eaveCm ≥ X.ridgeCm − 10`, `gable` when
   `X.ridgeCm > Y.ridgeCm + 10` (the end wall rises above `Y`'s roof), else `valley`; a free end is `hip` on a `hip`
   roof and `gable` on every other kind. A block's side partly shared with a piece's end is classed on the shared part.
2. **Ridge lines.** The base's ridge (for a `rect`, the midpoints of its ends; for a `quad`, the arc-length midpoints of
   the chains its `ridgeAxis` names, §2.6), with each end adjusted: `hip` pulls the ridge end inward along the ridge by
   `WingRoleRow.hipInset × span` (0.5 — the plan hip at equal pitches — for ranges; a block's `FM` entry, V02 §3.10.8's
   measured-rate cell, 0.25 until calibrated, keeps a ridge half its short side long, never a pyramid; the hip facets' own
   pitch then follows from the inset and the rise), collapsing to the centre only when the wing is no longer than
   `2 × hipInset × span`; `valley` extends it into `Y` by `valleyReach(X, Y, 'float')` (V02 §3.7); `gable`, `party`,
   `mitre`, `wall` and `open` leave it at the end's midpoint (a mitre end's midpoint is the path vertex).
3. **Facets per wing.** `gable` / `hip` roofs: the two long facets from each eave to the ridge, a hip triangle at each
   `hip` end; a `valley` end's facets continue into `Y` up to the **valley lines** — the plan projections of the lines
   where `X`'s facet planes meet `Y`'s near facet plane, clipped to `Y`'s footprint (where `X`'s eave is below `Y`'s, the
   valley starts inside `Y` on the line where `X`'s facet reaches `Y`'s eave height). `shed`: one facet from the low eave
   to the `high` side. `pyramid` and `cone`: one triangle per ring edge to the apex over the ring's centroid. **Pent band
   facets** (J-V2.75): for a wing `x` with a pent roof and the wing `y` standing on it — their rings concentric with equal
   insets and the same vertex count (ST3, ST4) — the facets are the band between the two rings: for each side `i` of `x`'s
   ring one planar facet from that side at `x.eaveCm` to the matching side `i` of `y`'s ring at `x.ridgeCm` (two parallel
   edges, so the facet is planar), neighbouring facets sharing the edge from `x`'s vertex to `y`'s matching vertex as
   their hip line; a round or octagonal ring is treated per edge (a cone's band); nothing is built inside `y`'s ring. So
   `ridgeCm = eaveCm + p × d` is exactly the height at which the skirt meets the wall of the tier above, and the casters and
   the glTF and CityJSON roofs read the same facets. A pent-kind roof on a wing with nothing standing on it (a truncated
   stack's former lower tier) is laid as the top's roof instead (ST4). `tent`: as a cone at its pitch; a spire is a
   `cone` or `pyramid` at its spire pitch. `flat`: one facet at eave height, with an inner parapet line where
   `parapetCm > 0`. `dome` (a template part's roof): four latitude bands of planar quads over the ring's area centroid
   (triangles at the apex), rise = the ring's mean radius × `domeRise` (1.0; own), each band's ring the base ring scaled
   toward the centroid by `cos` of its latitude (15°, 37.5°, 60°, 82.5° by `dmath`). `plain` (the F-SKELETON downgrade):
   one flat facet at eave height with no lines. `none` (the decline's roofless state): no facet — the wing is excluded
   from the tiling check below and drawn by §8.2's `states` rows. `skeleton` (a drawn footprint, a template polygon): the
   base's validated straight-skeleton faces (§3.8), with its plain-roof downgrade. **The cupola** (M12): a small solid at
   its range's ridge midpoint — a square plan of side `0.3 ×` the range's width, a drum of `0.25 ×` that side, and a
   `dome` (as above), a `tip` (a cone of rise 2 × its half side) or a `pyramid` — standing on the ridge; its facets are
   extra (`part: 'cupola'`), painted over the roof, never in `Heights`. Every facet vertex carries its height `z` (cm above
   the building's lowest `baseCm`), so each facet has an exact plane and normal.
   **Chimneys** (both kinds; §8.6, §8.10). A decorative chimney (no plan) at its host point of V02 §3.7, on its host's
   facet. A **plan chimney** (§2.6's `Chimney`, with a plan) is drawn on the roof or terrace facet over `Chimney.column` of
   the wing that holds storey `Chimney.levels[1]` and whose ring contains the column — so a lower tier's stack carried up
   through the tiers above (V03) rises from the top of the stack, never from a roof the tier above covers; a chimney whose
   column lies inside the ring of a wing standing on that wing (a stored plan not yet re-cut) is not drawn and is reported
   (`chimneyCovered`) until the plan re-derives its levels (V03).
4. **Occlusion, so facets never overlap.** Each valley region (the part of `X`'s extended facets inside `Y`) is removed
   from `Y`'s facets; each tower ring is removed from every other facet (a tower always covers what it overlaps —
   V02 §3.5 M11 guarantees its eave is above every roof it meets); each ring of a wing that stands on another is removed
   from the facets of the wing it stands on (V02 §5.6); a dormer's plan rectangle is removed from its host facet and
   replaced by the dormer's own facets (a `dormer` or `wallGable`: two facets from its front edge to a short ridge
   perpendicular to the host's, `depthShare` up the slope; a `hoist`: the same with a flat front; the `entranceGable`:
   two facets whose ridge runs to the host's ridge); the porches, outside the footprint, add their own facets (a hood: one
   thin facet; `gabled`, `twoStorey`: two facets with a ridge square to the wall; `halfRound`: the half-cone's triangles,
   one per arc segment, to the apex on the wall line; `recessed`: none — a notch line in the eave). The result tiles
   footprint ∪ porches, less the wings roofed `none` (T-V2-9); the cupola's facets lie over it and are excluded from the
   tiling.
5. **Lines.** Ridges, hips (the hip facets' shared edges and a mitre on its convex side), valleys (valley lines and a
   mitre on its concave side), eaves (the footprint outline, the base's), a `wall` end's line, tower seams (every other
   ring vertex's edge to the apex for a cone with 16 or more sides, every edge for a pyramid).
6. **Order.** Within a building: porch facets, then wing facets, then dormer facets, then tower facets, then all lines —
   the same painter's order the reference uses (porch under the eave, the tall parts last), which with non-overlapping
   facets only decides the order of anti-aliased edges. Wing facets go in stack order — a wing's before those of every
   wing standing on it.

The **surface layer** of §8.4 (a) takes its roofs from these facets (the "roof construction" it names), so the light
pass lights the true roof planes and the tower cones. **The shadow casters are the base wings' prisms** (V02 §3.14.1):
each wing's ring from `baseCm` to its eave, and its roof's rise over its ring (a tower's cone or spire only over its own
ring) — model heights, so **no shadow of the model's masses depends on a click** (J-V2.22); they are also item 102's epoch
casters, and never a generation-time caster. The surface-layer shading of the porches, the dormers and the cupola
(rungs 1–2 and the roof ornament) appears with their drawing — view only, in no digest and no caster.

### 5.3 Style rows and paint programs

`StyleSheet.roofConstruction`'s `'roofscape'` (§8.2; item 406) is the default construction of every shipped family from
stage 3's landing; the older constructions remain for the parity presets (under `MFCG` and `FTG` the massing is the
base's, and their sheets keep their constructions). Paint programs added to §8.2's list (each numeric parameter is a cell
of the program's entry in the sheet's `programs`, with its value in the table below):

* `roofscape(tone: 'twoTone' | 'mono' | 'facet')` — fills every facet in the `roof` role: `twoTone` by `faceLight` per
  facet (`lit`), `mono` one tone with the light pass's shading (`ink`, whose light is value-only, §8.4), `facet` the
  per-facet diffuse-and-specular shading of the reference look (the `FM` preset's building band; §8.4 (h), P24); then the
  lines of V02 §5.2 step 5 in `ink` at `ridgeWeight` (ridges and seams) and `hipWeight` (hips and valleys).
* `dormer` and `porch` — their facets through the same tone rule, outlined at `partWeight`; `towerRoof` — a cone's facets
  with the seam lines of step 5, a pyramid's with its hips, a spire's the same at its pitch; the cupola through
  `towerRoof` at `partWeight`.
* **Roof decorations** (§8.10 rows, view data, keyed by the render key): `sails` — a windmill's four sails on its tower's
  roof, turned to the settlement's prevailing wind where the site states one, else to `+y`; `smokeStack` — V02 §3.14.6's
  added decorative stacks; and, **only in the `FM` building look**, `stepStones` (a stone path from the main door to the
  frame's access side, stones `stoneM` at `stonePitchM`) and `wallGrass` (grass tufts at re-entrant corners); with the
  `FM` look's per-building roof hue (`weathering` on hue at `fmHueW`, §8.2) and cone facets doubled for drawing only.
* **V01's NG draw-style bars** (the `hatched` family's two tapers per wing, §13.5): the NG parity sheet's roof
  construction is V01 §5.1's sentence (X14).
* `hatch(ridge | eave, pitch, taper)` (§8.2): the `hatched` family's hatch program is V01's (V01 §5.1.2), run per
  roofscape facet; the `FM` look hatches parallel to the eave at the paper pitch `fmHatchPx`.
* The `lit` family's roof tint by band (§8.2, item 19) and the material's `pattern` (texture) apply per facet, never
  changing a facet (J-A19.42).
* The **contrast matrix** is unchanged: the roof role's pairs are the building role's (§8.2).

| cell (program) | value (own) | read by |
|---|---|---|
| `ridgeWeight` (`roofscape`, `towerRoof` seams) | ½ of the band's building outline weight | the line pass of step 5 |
| `hipWeight` (`roofscape`) | ⅓ of the band's building outline weight | hips and valleys |
| `partWeight` (`dormer`, `porch`, the cupola's `towerRoof`) | ½ of the band's building outline weight | their outlines |
| `stoneM`, `stonePitchM` (`stepStones`, §8.10) | stones 0.5–0.8 m, at 1 m pitch | the `FM` look's path |
| `fmHueW` (the `FM` look's roof hue) | 0.15 | §8.2's `weathering` on hue |
| `fmHatchPx` (`hatch`, the `FM` look) | 0.9 px at 1× | the `FM` hatch |
| `treadWeight`, `treadStopShare`, `treadMinPx` (`stairFlight`, V02 §5.6) | ⅓ of the band's building outline weight; 0.1 of the flight's width at each side; 2 px of plan per tread | the tread lines |

### 5.4 Labels

Stage 3 adds **no** `LabelTable` row and no S13b candidate: a building keeps the base's labels (a landmark's point label
at its footprint, an address). The room labels are the base's (§8.5, from the plan rung). Hovering a wing at the
district band and finer names it — its role in our own words from the naming slice **`building.wingRole`** (one entry per
`WingRole`, authored in V11's naming tables, X6: "the main range", "the gate range", "a cross-wing", "a pavilion", "a rear
range", "a service range", "a tower", "a stair turret", "a part", "a shelter"; the role id is the fallback) and the
building's name — through the reader (§11.2), under the building's `knownTo` (§9.2); nothing here is concealed. An
`ovalCourt`'s solid ranges hover as "the seating" and its `gate` passage wings as "a gate passage" (two entries of the
slice, keyed by the family and the wing's `solid` flag; X6).

### 5.5 Exports (item 449)

| format | stage 3 adds |
|---|---|
| **JSON schema** | per building a `massing` block (family, row, grammar, entrance hint, `segments`, `low`, `cupola`; each wing's key, role, kind, ring, heights, roof, `arcade`) and, where the `wings` rung is current or stored, a `composition` block with its state (as the base's `plan` block): row, grammar, composed wings (`base`, dormer rows with their derived positions), towers (`base`), the porch and the secondary porch with their derived rings, the courts (derived rings), the rooms; round-trips (T-V2-24) |
| **SVG** | at the district band and finer, §11.1's grouping: the roofscape's facets in the semantics `sem.building.roof` (wing facets), `sem.building.roof.dormer`, `sem.building.roof.porch`, `sem.building.roof.tower` and `sem.building.roof.cupola` (by `RoofFacet.part`), and V02 §5.2 step 5's lines in `sem.building.roofline`, each group one compound `<path>` per (semantic, district), the groups in V02 §5.2 step 6's order; the `<metadata>` map carries each facet's subpath range to its wing address `wing:<building>/<key>` (a porch's to its building, a cupola's to its range's wing) — no per-building group and no `data-wing` attribute, so §12.7's element budgets hold; at the city band nothing new (masses) |
| **glTF 2.0 / OBJ** | roofs from the roofscape facets (replacing per-wing roof meshes), towers as ring prisms with cone, pyramid or spire facets, the cupola as a small mesh; an `arcade` wing's ground storey exported open (its piers as four corner prisms, its walls from the first storey); with compositions: dormers and porches as small meshes; `extras` carry each wing's key and role. The export option `compositions`: `asDrawn` (the default) — the compositions whose rung is current or stored; `derive` — `compose()` run for every building of the export scope first, in the derivation pool, under V02 §6.4's export budget; `none` — the massing only |
| **CityJSON 2.0** | LoD2.2 `RoofSurface` per roofscape facet, `WallSurface` from the wing prisms, dormers and porches as their own surfaces when compositions are exported; semantics attributes `plat:role` and `plat:key` in the `Plat` extension (§11.1's `plat.ext.json`) |
| **GeoJSON** | an optional `wings` layer (strict and metric variants): one Polygon per base wing with `key`, `role`, `floors`, `eaveCm`, `ridgeCm`, `roof`, `building`; the base's building features carry `onDeck`, `deck` and a stepped building's `tiers` (item 447), and the `wings` layer repeats none of them |
| **VTT** | unchanged at the ground scene (footprint walls, the base's); a tower's ring is part of the footprint's walls; the storey scenes are the plan's (V03) |

### 5.6 Stacks, stairs and deck buildings on the map

* **Bands.** City band: the footprint (tier 0 ∪ stair 0, and any ground wings added beside it) as a mass like any
  other. District band and finer: the roofscape with the stack's occlusion and order (V02 §5.2 steps 4 and 6) — terraces
  as flat facets with their parapet lines, pent skirts as their band facets meeting the wall of the tier above (V02 §5.2
  step 3), the top's roof or the shrine's, each stair's shed facet painted by `stairFlight`; a sealed stack (`none`)
  draws no stair; chimneys only on exposed roof (V02 §3.7, V02 §5.2). An `ovalCourt` draws its façade ring's flat roofs with
  their parapet lines and its seating ring's shed facets falling toward the floor, which is drawn as a court (a yard
  part). Neighbourhood and building bands: V02 §5.1's, the plan per storeyed tier (V03).
* **`stairFlight`** (a paint program added to §8.2's list with item 406's): the stair's facet filled by the roofscape's
  tone rule (its slope lit by `faceLight` like any facet), with tread lines across the flight, perpendicular to its
  climb, by `stairTreads` (V02 §2.6): `n − 1` lines at `goingCm` intervals from the foot, in `ink` at `treadWeight`,
  stopping short of each side by `treadStopShare` of the flight's width; below `treadMinPx` of plan per tread the lines
  are omitted and the shaded facet reads as a ramp.
* **The surface layer and the shadows.** Each wing's facets enter §8.4's surface layer at their true heights (a terrace
  at its deck level, a stair's slope), so the light pass lights every terrace and step face; the casters are the wings'
  prisms from their own `baseCm` (V02 §3.15.3), kept current on every re-basing path by `rebaseStack` (V02 §3.15.2), so
  each tier's shadow falls on the terrace or the ground below it; under a Works, the stage heights of item 318.
* **The per-wing constructions** (the parity presets' sheets, and the base outline builder's drawing from M3a until the
  roofscape lands at M6a): a wing that stands on another is drawn after it, its ring clipping the lower wing's roof, and a
  stair's shed with its treads (item 419).
* **Labels.** No new `LabelTable` row. Hovering names the roles from `building.wingRole` (X6, with "a tier", "the
  shrine", "a stair"). A deck building keeps the base's labels.
* **Exports** (V02 §5.5's rows, extended): **JSON** — each wing's `on` and `solid`, the massing block's `stack`, and for a
  deck building a derived `deck` block (`kind`, `host`) read from its plot at export; **glTF / OBJ** — each wing extruded
  from its own `baseCm` (a tier stands on the tier below at its deck level), a solid tier as a closed prism, each stair as
  a stepped solid of `stairTreads`' `n` risers (the k-th top at `⌊k × rise ÷ n⌋`) and treads of `goingCm`, the head tread
  taking the remainder; **CityJSON 2.0** — tier 0 is the `Building`, each tier above and the shrine a `BuildingPart` with
  LoD2.2 surfaces (a terrace a `RoofSurface`, the walls `WallSurface`s from the part's own base), each stair a
  `BuildingInstallation` (an outer stair, stepped by `stairTreads`) with `plat:role 'stair'` (J-V2.77); **GeoJSON**'s
  `wings` layer — `on`, `solid` and `baseCm` per wing; **VTT** — the ground scene's walls from the footprint (the base's),
  a stair's outer sides not walls. A deck building exports as any building, its `baseCm` the deck's.

## 6 Performance budgets

Every number here is **PLAUSIBLE** (an estimate from operation counts on §12.1's reference machine) until the
measurements named below; each has its pre-decided fallback. The building counts per rung are §1.1's, the first-map
times §12.5's. The mix is §2.6's assumed core mix (its cost note): about 55 % row quads, 25 % single ranges, 18 % tiled
multi-wing massings, 2 % with towers.

### 6.1 The massing (eager, on the first map's path)

| building kind | massing cost per building (median; PLAUSIBLE) | basis |
|---|---|---|
| row (pass-through, heights, roof, a back range where drawn) | 1–3 µs | one frame, one rect, M11–M13 on ≤ 2 wings |
| single range | 3–6 µs | frame, `lir`, one slab, snap and checks |
| tiled families (`L`, `T`, `H`, `U`, `cross`, `rectCourt`, `gridWalk`), blocks included | 15–40 µs | ≤ 8 slabs, the pairing check (§2.6 rule 4 (ii)), ≤ 4 block trials |
| `plotRing` and the fantasy families | 30–60 µs | simplification, line offsets, mitres, angle checks |
| with towers or a turret | + 20–60 µs | per trial: a ring (≤ 24 vertices), its overlap share by the kernel's boolean on the arrangement, the seed-contract distances |
| an F-MASSING attempt | × (1 + attempts) | ≤ 3 attempts of the drawn family, then one per other family |

**Bars (the stage-3 intake, item 223):** town-wide median ≤ **10 µs** per building (the base's admission bound; the
estimate is ≈ 3 µs, rows dominating); for the composed classes (every building whose family is not `row`, `single`,
`shelter` or `baseOutline`) median ≤ **60 µs** and p99 ≤ **250 µs**; mean over all buildings ≤ **12 µs**. S11's §12.4 row
is re-declared by the measured difference (the estimate: mean + 6 µs per building).

| rung (at its target, §1.1) | added massing CPU | added first-map wall time (3 pool workers) | share of §12.5's first map |
|---|---|---|---|
| TOWN | ≈ 9 ms | ≈ 3 ms (≈ 9 ms single-threaded) | ≈ 2–6 % |
| CITY | ≈ 36 ms | ≈ 12 ms | ≈ 3 % |
| METROPOLIS | ≈ 90 ms | ≈ 30 ms | ≈ 3 % |
| the 120 000 cap | ≈ 216 ms | ≈ 72 ms | ≈ 3 % |

**Measurement** (M6a; T-V2-22): the massing timed per class on B-CITY's TOWN, CITY and METROPOLIS seeds, 20 runs, and the
first-map time re-measured. **Pre-decided fallbacks, in order, each a declared shift (§13.3):** (a) M8's candidate trials
capped at 6 per building and M14's rung 0 at one attempt for the composed classes; (b) towers and turrets off in the
massing (the families kept; the rows' tower cells read 0), re-measured; (c) the base's own intake fallback (§2.6): the base
outline builder makes the outline and `compose()` works inside it (the composer then adds only dormer rows and the porch)
— reported as "stage-3 massing withdrawn at this rung" for the owner's veto (D-18).

### 6.2 The composer, the rooms rung and the roofscape (lazy)

| work | budget | estimate | when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compose(…, 'wings')` per building | median ≤ **0.2 ms**, p95 ≤ 0.6 ms (inside §12.7's per-building bound) | 20–150 µs: `facadeBays` per eave against the wings it meets, ≤ 2 rows per wing, one porch ray on the plot's rings, ≤ 10 draws | a neighbourhood click, a building click, a `view` tile request |
| `facadeBays` on every side (the lit windows before a plan), `stairTreads`, `cryptSeedWings` | ≤ 10 µs per wing for every side; ≤ 2 µs per call for the other two | a side's run against ≤ 16 meeting rings in integer arithmetic; one ceiling and one floor division; one pass over ≤ 16 wings | §8.4's lit windows at a night view; the drawing and exports of stairs; §2.6's basement function |
| a neighbourhood click (≈ 300–600 buildings; §12.6's district ceiling) | §12.7's pool time per tile, amortised; the whole neighbourhood within ≤ 120 ms of pool time, streamed centre-out | ≈ 45 ms of pool time (the ceiling × 0.1 ms) | II.4's click |
| `compose(…, 'rooms')` per building | ≤ 0.3 ms median | ≤ 4 rectangles and one ring difference per tower storey | with the plan, on the building click |
| `roofscape` per building | ≤ 25 µs median, ≤ 150 µs p99 (a large manor) | end classes O(wings²) with wings ≤ 16, facets, float64 occlusion clips | the tile worker, per building per (leaf digest, composition hash, construction) — memoised as the base's derived-roof cache (§8.1 item 5) |
| a district-band tile's roofscape | ≤ 8 ms of tile-worker raster time for ≤ 400 buildings | 400 × 20 µs | inside §8.8's per-tile raster budget |
| `compose()` under `elaborate: 'view'` per tile (§12.7's pool time per tile, amortised) | only tiles **at the neighbourhood band and finer** request the `wings` rung (the district band draws the massing's roofscape and requests nothing); p95 buildings per neighbourhood-band tile at the METROPOLIS core ≤ 60 → ≈ 12 ms at 0.2 ms each | ≤ 60 × 0.2 ms ≈ 12 ms (measured at M6b on B-CITY METROPOLIS) | a pan under `view` |

**Measurement** (M6b): on B-CITY METROPOLIS, compose per building by class, 50 neighbourhood clicks, 200 district-band
tiles, and the buildings per neighbourhood-band tile at the core (p95). **Fallbacks:** a tile's `view` request over its
pool time is sliced into batches of at most `viewBatchMs` (16 ms of pool time) streamed centre-out, the tile drawing the
massing's roofscape until each batch lands, reported (J-V2.53); a compose median over 0.2 ms: the porch's space test runs
on the plot's ring only (the other footprints ignored, the porch then clipped at draw); still over §12.7's per-building
bound: the dormer rows drop to one per wing (the street eave), reported. A roofscape over budget per tile: the valley
extensions are drawn without the occlusion clip (the abutting wing's valley triangles overpainted in order), a declared
view shift.

### 6.3 Memory

* **Model:** per building ≈ 36 B for roles, keys, `nextWingKey` and `MassingRef` (with `segments`, `low` and `cupola`),
  and ≈ 50 B for the extra wings the composed massings carry (about 1.8 wings per building instead of about 1.3) —
  ≈ 1.2 MB at the METROPOLIS target, counted in §12.8's model line and re-declared at the intake.
* **The elaboration cache:** a `wings`-rung chunk ≤ **1 KB** per building at p99 (§12.8's line) — its composed wings and
  towers are key references (2 B each), dormer rows 8 B each, the porch 12 B; the `rooms` rung's rings are counted in the
  plan's per-storey line (§12.8; a tower room's ring is encoded as its tower's index and storey, derived at decode).
  Measured at M6b on B-PLAN's fixtures and B-CITY; fallback: §12.8's (the cap halves).
* **The roofscape memo:** ≤ 2 KB per building in the tile worker's session memo, LRU-capped at 8 MB per worker, evicting
  to recomputation.

### 6.4 Edits and exports

* `setMassing` dry run and commit: ≤ 2 ms per edit (one plot's S11 re-fit, the checks, the carry); `setComposition`
  ≤ 1 ms; the mutator's wing step ≤ 150 µs per building plus S11's re-fit — inside §12.6's per-edit laws, which count
  them.
* **Exports at METROPOLIS:** glTF / OBJ / CityJSON with `compositions: 'asDrawn'` ≤ 10 s in the generation worker (roofs
  ≈ 8–60 triangles per building, ≈ 0.4 M triangles); with `'derive'` ≤ 12 s (compose for 15 000 buildings ≈ 1.5 s of pool
  time); a district-band SVG ≤ 1.5 KB per building. **Measured** at M6b; **fallback:** `derive` streams district by
  district with the dialog's progress; if still over, METROPOLIS exports default to `asDrawn` and label `derive` "slow",
  reported.

### 6.5 Stacks and deck buildings

| work | budget | estimate (PLAUSIBLE) |
|---|---|---|
| the massing of a `stepped` building (`massStepped`: ST0–ST8, at most three attempts) | ≤ 120 µs p99, inside the composed classes' ≤ 250 µs p99 (V02 §6.1) | ≤ 9 tiers × (an inset, a stair, the containment and the sibling-disjointness tests) ≈ 20–60 µs, plus §2.6 rule 4 (iii)'s union check over ≤ 20 wings ≈ 20–40 µs; a second or third attempt only on a `TierFailure` |
| the massing of an `ovalCourt` (`massOval`) | ≤ 150 µs p99 | two line-offset passes over ≤ 20 edges (as `plotRing`), ≤ 40 quads, the pairing check ≈ 40–90 µs; at most one or two arenas per city |
| `rebaseStack` on a terrain stroke, a warp step or a crypt lift | ≤ 20 µs per stepped building | O(wings) samples and one pass in stack order; counted inside §12.6's per-stroke law with the base's per-entity re-basing |
| how many | stepped buildings are landmarks: ≤ 0.1 % of buildings at every rung (V11's caps, X17), so V02 §6.1's town-wide median and mean do not move | — |
| a deck building's massing | a single range's (V02 §6.1) | — |
| the roofscape of a stepped building | ≤ 60 µs | facets on ≤ 20 wings with the stacked occlusion |
| a `tiers` edit or a tier's height edit | ≤ 2 ms (V02 §6.4's `setMassing` line) | one anchored `layTiers`, the re-base and the re-lay |
| the carry check of a stepped building inside a warp (item 333) | ≤ 40 µs per building per halving, counted like V02 §8.4 R5's towered buildings | the union and the containment tests |

**Measurement** at M6a on B-MASS's stepped and deck sub-fixtures (T-V2-22's harness), and at M3a for the base outline
builder's lay. **Fallbacks, in order:** ST6's containment tests run on the rings' bounding boxes first and the exact test
only on an overlap (a pure speed-up, no output change); then tiers above seven truncated at ST3 (a declared shift,
§13.3).

| family shares (`regularCourt`, `starCourt`, `chordArc`, `rectCourt`, `gridWalk`) | 8 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 9 of 41 — consistent with equal odds (χ² 0.34, df 4) | χ² against equal shares, p ≥ 0.05 |

| blocks per building | 0 ×16, 1 ×20, 2 ×3, 3 ×2 (mean 0.78) | mean within ± 25 % |
| towers per building | 0 ×15, 1 ×22, 2 ×3, 3 ×1 (mean 0.76; ≥ 1 in 63 %) | mean within ± 25 %; the ≥ 1 share within ± 15 points |
| **square towers** (on blocks) among typed towers | 9 / 29 | the share within ± 15 points (candidate (d)'s `towerOnBlock` calibrated) |
| dormer elements per **segment** | 1.61 | within ± 25 % |
| porch elements per building | 0 ×17, 1 ×14, 2 ×9, 3 ×1 | the share with a porch (24 / 41 = 59 %) within ± 15 points; buildings with two or more porches (10 / 41) **reported**, not gating (our secondary porch is a hood at a side, rear or yard door; J-V2.44) |

## 8 Build plan

### 8.1 Where stage 3 sits in §16's order

Stage 3 is built as **milestone M6**, after M5 (stage 2), in three parts (item 524), in the combined order J122 decided
(§16's staged-milestones table; INDEX §4). It depends on: M2b (roofs, the `lit` family, compound site plans, the
designation templates and the generation fill); M3a (the designation mutator with its record and inverse, assignments,
the dry run and bending, the handle-based API); M3b (the glTF, OBJ and CityJSON exporters); M4 (Works and the evolution
hooks the mutation steps feed); M5 (the neighbourhood click of II.4 that raises the `wings` rung — **decoupled**: without
M5 the rung is raised by a building click and by `elaborate: 'view'`, so M6 does not wait on M5's gate); **V11's
compiled templates (V11 C1–C3b; C3b's `fort` and `arena` families at M3a)** — the template families, the class roster
with `templateFamily`, the `HeightsRow` with item 427's columns and the role table — **before M6a** (the chain and
T-V2-33 read them); **V04's access draw** (its T2b stage) before T-V2-36's dig and crypt parts; the crypt derivation
(M6-U: items 238, 226 and 436) before T-V2-36's crypt part. **The plan rung (V03) runs before M6** under the decided
order (V03 §11 Q1, J122): its P0, P1 and P3 run on the base's wings after M4 and take the composer's rooms and dormer
rows when M6b lands (V03 §8; §16's M6-P row, item 567); this volume's `facadeBays`, `endMarginM` and `bayM` are therefore built first, after M4
and before V03's P1, in `@plat/plots` (item 505), as M6b's item moved forward and priced in M6b's estimate (V03 §3.6's
W2 imports them and prices none). V06 reads the recorded wing steps from **M6a**.

## 9 Decisions

Each row is final unless the owner or the Fable retrovalidation vetoes it; each is "chose X over Y because Z". A row
that a later row changed carries one mark — "superseded by" or "amended by" that row (E-24) — and the governing row keeps
the reason.

| id | decision |
|---|---|
| J-V2.1 | Chose to make stage 3's **massing the eager `outline()` at S11** (model data: the footprint, heights, shadows and capacity read it) over keeping the base outline and composing only lazily, because the owner's buildings must show their composed plan — courts, cross-wings, towers — at every zoom with one footprint hash across LOD (O17 (i)), and the massing costs ≈ 3 % of the first map (V02 §6.1). |
| J-V2.2 | Chose to let the **massing own every height and ring**, the composer never re-shaping a wing or changing a covered storey, over using the base contract's allowance for taller composed sections, because shadows, the 3-D export and the capacity must never depend on a click (§6.2: a click changes no digest). |
| J-V2.3 | Chose **tiled ranges and blocks** (butt joints at right angles, mitres otherwise; a block splits the range it straddles) over Fantasy Manor's overlapping blocks, because tiling keeps §2.6's cheap pairing tier and an exact capacity; **towers overlap** (tier (iii)) because a round ring cannot tile a rectangle without non-rectangular wings. Item 59's ADOPTED block/tower distinction holds — **a block's roof is always a hip, never a pyramid** (its ridge ends inset by `WingRoleRow.hipInset` × span — under `FM` the measured-rate entry of V02 §3.10.8), and **the square pyramids are towers standing on blocks** (M8's candidate (d), contained in its block, weight 0 by default and calibrated under `FM`). |
| J-V2.4 | Chose to put **towers and turrets first in wing order** over path order, so §2.6's clip order takes each tower whole (a round room per storey) and each range less its towers, and no seed piece has a hole. |
| J-V2.5 | Chose to keep Fantasy Manor's **regular, star and arc families behind the `fantasyShapes` model toggle, off by default**, over its equal weights as the default, because the owner adopted "realism in the base, fantasy as toggles" (D-7); the `FM` preset turns them on at the reference's weights. |
| J-V2.6 | Chose **composed wings and towers that name their base wing by key and store no ring** over storing composed rings, because one geometry source removes a class of carry bugs (the write that survives one path and ghosts another) and makes a mutation's re-match trivial. |
| J-V2.7 | Chose **dormers and gables that never project past the eave** — a projecting bay is a block, which the footprint shows — over Fantasy Manor's projecting cross-gables, because a projection would leave the footprint (the stage-3 contract) and possibly the plot (item 59). |
| J-V2.8 | Chose **orientation by the frontage and fitting in the frontage-aligned largest inscribed rectangle of the slot hint** (`plotRing` following the hint itself) over a random rotation or a free fit in the plot's OBB, because item 59 keeps our plot rule and a building must never leave its plot. |
| J-V2.9 | Chose to derive the **`rooms` rung only with the plan** over deriving it under `view`, because nothing but the plan draws it and its cost would be wasted on a pan. |
| J-V2.10 | Chose **per-wing keyed composition draws** (creation index from the wing's key) over per-building draws, so every wing a mutation keeps recomposes byte for byte without storing the composition — item 18's "keep what fits" by construction. |
| J-V2.11 | Chose to **lay a mutation's target family around the kept ranges** (the growth lattice, anchored mode) over re-running the family and matching after, because item 18 (a) wants "the old house still recognisable inside the new workshop". |
| J-V2.12 | Chose to **draw a mutation's target family** on `siteplan.mutate` over the reachable, feasible families over taking the heaviest, for variety across a town; the stream keeps it deterministic and reversible. |
| J-V2.13 | Chose to **keep a row building's quads** through every designation change that keeps the `row` arrangement (only its back range and storeys change) over re-laying rows, because the quad is the plot's (shared party walls) and item 31's geometry floor protects built stock. A change to a `compound` arrangement keeps the quad byte-identical as the compound's frontage slot and adds the target's main structure behind it (V02 §3.9 W3b). |
| J-V2.14 | Chose a **back range by band** for rows, houses and cottages over leaving rows unarticulated, because rear ranges on burgage plots are the historical norm, the yard behind stays (the coverage cap), and it carries item 19's "scale in structure" to the commonest building. |
| J-V2.15 | Chose **porch kinds filtered by the free space in front of the door** — a flush front takes a recessed porch or none — over Fantasy Manor's porch lottery, because no porch may stand over a street. |
| J-V2.16 | Chose **a closed ring with a gate hall** (the court a footprint hole, reached through the front range) over an open ring spanned above, which would need an in-plot passage face, because item 30's passages are block-level and courtyard houses and inns were entered through a gate hall. |
| J-V2.17 | Chose **two event kinds with op unions** (`setMassing`, `setComposition`) over one event kind per operation, keeping item 101's small vocabulary and one dry-run path per kind. |
| J-V2.18 | Chose **geometric edits that draw nothing** — an omitted value takes the row's central value — over drawn defaults, so the tool behaves predictably; the `setMassing` `family` op is a designation mutation and **draws on `siteplan.mutate`** exactly as one (V02 §3.12), replayable because that stream is a pure function of its key. |
| J-V2.19 | Chose to **switch the composed massing off under the `MFCG` and `FTG` presets** (the base outline) over composing under them, so §13.5's parity rows stay on the references' behaviour (item 23). |
| J-V2.20 | Chose a **building-scope `FM` preset whose element rates are calibrated to Fantasy Manor's measured outputs**, not copied from its code, over a constant table taken from the code reading, because §17.1's clean room admits the code only for understanding, while emulation-first (item 23) still wants the reference's behaviour reproducible. |
| J-V2.21 | Chose **one planar, non-overlapping roof plan per building** (the roofscape) drawn and exported by one function over independent per-wing roofs painted in order, because valleys, walls and towers come out right, the light pass gets exact normals, and the exports agree with the picture. |
| J-V2.22 | Chose to keep the **shadow casters on the model's wing prisms** over casting from composition parts, so **no shadow of the model's masses depends on a click**; the surface-layer shading of a porch, the dormers and the cupola appears with their drawing — view only, no digest. |
| J-V2.23 | Chose to **repair the size budget by scaling and dropping parts**, never by asking for land, over a JOIN inside the massing, because land is S10's and the mutator's and the massing must stay a per-slot pure function. |
| J-V2.24 | Chose a **second admission bound for the composed classes** (≤ 60 µs median, ≤ 250 µs p99) beside the base's town-wide 10 µs median, over one 10 µs bound per class, because the composed classes are a few per cent of buildings and inherently heavier, while the town-wide median and the mean bound the first map. |
| J-V2.25 | Chose **one façade-bay rhythm** (`facadeBays`) for dormers, the plan's windows, lit windows before a plan and decorative chimneys over separate spacing rules, so the picture stays consistent when the plan arrives. |
| J-V2.26 | Chose to **raise a tower's eave above every roof it overlaps** over a per-pixel height sort, so plan occlusion is a subtraction and every tower reads as rising through the roofs, as towers do. |
| J-V2.27 | Chose a **separate `@plat/buildings` package** between `plots` and `labels` over folding the composer into `@plat/plots`, keeping S11 small and the interface (in `plots`) apart from its implementation. |
| J-V2.28 | Chose a new roof kind **`shed`** over drawing lean-tos and outshots as gables, for realism on the commonest additions and on lean-to shelters (item 70). |
| J-V2.29 | Chose **tower ring side counts by radius** (12 / 16 / 24) over one count, so a small turret keeps its sides above `minEdge` and a great tower looks round. |
| J-V2.30 | Chose **V11's four anchor bands (poor, modest, prosperous, rich) with V11's derivation for squalid and comfortable** for every row of `composition.json` over three anchors with midpoints, so **one band-anchoring rule serves every template-like table** and the massing bends where the size budget bends. |
| J-V2.31 | Chose to **measure the porch's space on the building's own plot** over the neighbourhood around it, so the rung stays a function of its building and plot (§4.1's contract). |
| J-V2.32 | Chose **M6 after M5 in three parts, the massing first** (with the roofscape) over the composer first, because the massing is on the first map and is what every view shows; the plan rung (V03) runs before M6 under the decided order (V03 §11 Q1) — its P0, P1 and P3 on the base's wings after M4, taking the composer's rooms and dormer rows when M6b lands — so this volume's `facadeBays`, `endMarginM` and `bayM` are built first, priced in M6b (V02 §8.1). Amended by J122. |
| J-V2.33 | Chose **V11's family-keyed `HeightsRow`**, with V02 supplying three columns (`attic`, `parapetCm`, `towerStoreyCm`, item 427), and **one pitch rule** (`roofPitch × ClimateRow.roof.pitch ÷ pitchRef`, clamped) over V02's own class-keyed heights row and a climate-only pitch, because one content owner and one key avoid a second source of truth, and the climate still steepens or flattens every family's roof. |
| J-V2.34 | Chose **one resolution chain** — the template's key, a class override, a village class map, the template family, a full default per arrangement; for other slots the slot's key, the role key, `outbuilding` — with **rows per V11 template family and per structure role**, class rows only as overrides, and an **arrangement law checked at load**, over rows per class, because the roster has ~180 classes plus generic, custom and village ones while their shapes follow V11 §3.6.1's template families (35), and a row that contradicts its arrangement must never be read. |
| J-V2.35 | Chose a **slot-level size band** (`[p10, p90] × footprintShare ÷ count × buildingScale × sizeFactor`, the p10/p90 ratios **V11 §3.6.1's derivation ratios, mirrored as `sizeBandLo`/`sizeBandHi` (0.7 / 1.45, fixed)**, over 0.75 / 1.35), an **M3 least-footprint budget test** and an **M10 shrink that lowers the clamps and then falls down the reverse lattice**, over scaling alone, because the clamps undid the scale and T-V2-29 and T-V2-30 could not both pass; and read the **manor override** that V11 §3.6.1 carries (prosperous 420 m², rich 650 m², plot 3 000 m², main share ≥ 0.6; J-V11.39) for the owner's "giant manor … bigger courts". |
| J-V2.36 | Chose to read **the composer's rooms at the occupants' band**, emit the hall and chapel only for the `house` unit form or a programme hall, and clamp the hall to its programme row, over rooms fixed at the built band, because item 28 (f) keeps the shell and lets the interior follow who lives there. |
| J-V2.37 | Chose **the range opposite the gate as a closed ring's `main`**, the hall entered by a court door where the main door opens into the gate hall, over leaving closed families without a `main`, because courtyard houses and inns had their hall across the court from the gate. |
| J-V2.38 | Chose a **sunlit bias on the mirror coins** (`sunBias` 0.7; 0.5 in the parity presets `MFCG`, `FTG`, `VG` and `FM`, each with its own entry) over fair coins, because item 102 (d)'s "the rich seek the sun" reaches the building's garden and court side, and historical houses turned their courts to the south; the frontage orientation is never changed, and the bias is not scaled by band (passive orientation was common at every band). |
| J-V2.39 | Chose that **only a wing the mutator adds** over a sealed void draws for an access (keyed by its wing), that a `setMassing` op draws none (the user declares `addUndergroundAccess`), and that a replacement draws as new, over drawing on every massing change, because growth by new foundations is the owner's "more digging" while a hand edit must stay predictable. |
| J-V2.40 | Chose **the rear side by the outward normal away from the access**, independent of the ridge, over "the eave side farther from access", because the ridge is decided later and a gable-fronted row's eave sides are its party walls. |
| J-V2.41 | Chose **two orientation laws beside the frontage** (`fallLine` for the longhouse, `water` for mills and landings) over frontage-only orientation, because V07's longhouse rule is hard and a mill's wheel must stand on its water (realism tiebreaker). |
| J-V2.42 | Chose **attached structures** (a wheel, sails, a church's west tower and porch, a court institution's ranges) laid by the main slot's massing over separate slots, because they are parts of one building historically and a separate slot could not touch its host (item 304). |
| J-V2.43 | Chose to **shift the geometry value by the use's significance** (half a band per doubling, at most one band up, never down) over ignoring it, because a landmark or a weighty custom institution must read larger (item 104) while a weak one never shrinks built stock. |
| J-V2.44 | Chose **one main porch plus an optional secondary hood** (0 by default, calibrated under `FM`; buildings with two or more porches reported against the reference's 10 / 41) over the reference's up-to-three porches at any door, because historical houses mostly had one porch at the main door; recorded as a departure. |
| J-V2.45 | Chose to add the **half-round porch at weight 0 in the default rows** over a default weight, because it is Fantasy Manor's commonest porch but rare in the realism base; the `FM` preset calibrates it. |
| J-V2.46 | Chose a **raised-choir crypt** (the crypt's floor above the water table, the ground wings over the basement's ring lifted by `crypt.clearCm`) over exempting the cathedral from the water table (a crypt that floods) or a refusal (a cathedral with no crypt), because the owner's "the cathedral always has a crypt" is unconditional and a raised choir over a crypt is the historical answer on wet ground (J111). Amended by J-V2.108. |
| J-V2.47 | Chose **our own ids** (`regularCourt`, `starCourt`, `chordArc`, `rectCourt`, `gridWalk`) with a table-migration row over the reference's layout routine names, because §17.1's clean room forbids transferring its identifiers. |
| J-V2.48 | Chose **a canonical wing order (towers first, then by key) and wing references by key** (item 225) over index references, because V02's edits add and remove wings and an index would silently re-point a stored door or room. |
| J-V2.49 | Chose **the cupola as a massing draw recorded on `MassingRef`**, drawn from the district band and never in `Heights`, over a composition-rung ornament, because landmarks need their silhouettes before any click (NG C2) while shadows and capacity must not change. |
| J-V2.50 | Chose to express **the cross plan, the kiln, the chapter house and the tower on a block** with the existing constructions (`cross` as a main range with a two-piece cross slab; kilns and chapter houses as rangeless `towerHouse`s; the block tower as a contained square) over new wing kinds, keeping one geometry vocabulary. |
| J-V2.51 | Chose to answer "why this shape" through **V10's existing `WhyAnswer` fields** (alternatives as fact rows, recomputed without advancing a stream) over a new typed field, so no volume-10 change is needed. |
| J-V2.52 | Chose a **narrow `wingsInputs` digest** (the base wings, the main entrance, the massing reference, the slices, the porch's neighbourhood) over the building's whole leaf digest, because dormers and porches read nothing else and a relet must not mark a town stale at every epoch. ## 11 Owner questions

**Q-V2-1 — Should SettlementForge be able to prescribe a building's shape?** Answered **not now** (J122,
`docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-DELEGATED-2026-09-29.md`; vetoable), following SettlementForge's own product decisions (J121): the
truth runs one way and SettlementForge holds no shape data. The dossier says that an institution exists and what it is
(item 20); its building's plan — a courtyard, an H, towers — is the map's own construction (item 20 (h)), and the port
reads no shape field (V08). A map user fixes a layout with an assignment's drift bounds (`DriftBounds.families`,
V02 §2.1) or reshapes it with the building tool (V02 §4).

No other owner question arises: the owner's rules this volume applies (items 101 R2, 102–110, J111) are ruled, and every
other choice is a vetoable decision of V02 §9. The one choice the owner sees directly — the stepped temple's summit
standing 2.4–4.4 m behind its centre (J-V2.61) — is shown to his panel (V02 §7.5 (3)), reversible toward stairs cut into
the tiers if he vetoes it.
